actions.reason: read_observation decoded and validated the full receipt JSON on every call, even when the receipt text was identical to one it had already read (for example, while polling the receipt). Validation depends only on the text, apart from the ownership token comparison. The decode and validation steps move into _validated(text). Its result, either the checked fields or None for a malformed receipt, is kept in a module dict keyed by the receipt text and capped at 1024 entries. The dict is cleared when it is full. The symlink check, read_text and the ownership token comparison still run on every call. Each returned observation gets fresh copies of the remaining_processes list and the cpu_stat, memory.events and pids.events dicts, so callers never share mutable state with the cache. Accepted receipts, rejected receipts and the exception handling are unchanged.

Three edits, 44 changed lines.

This is my own measurement, not a verdict.

I now believe validation here depends only on the receipt text, apart from the token check. That makes it safe to reuse.
